newsitem.title: FRANCE: Corsican petrol stations suffer in farmer protest.
newsitem.headline: Corsican petrol stations suffer in farmer protest.

text.p: French paramilitary police used teargas on Friday to eject protesting farmers who had occupied Corsica's two petrol depots to press demands for a re-scheduling of debts and other issues, officials said.
All 180 petrol stations on the French Mediterranean island have been closed since Thursday night in protest at the farmers' seizure of the depots in Bastia and Ajaccio on Tuesday

At the Vazzio depot in the island capital Ajaccio, several farmers refused to obey police orders and the gendarmerie used teargas to disperse them. Two demonstrators were ejected by the fire brigade, apparently after suffering injuries, and several farmers were detained by police.
At the Marana depot at Bastia, police said no one was injured when they forced about 50 farmers to leave.
Officials said a delegation of farmers would meet officials at the Agriculture Ministry in Paris on Monday.
The petrol station owners association said earlier they were closing their outlets because they had "had enough of being taken hostage" each time a social problem erupted on the island.
The stations had been forced to close for several days in December when a lorry-drivers' strike blocked roads and prevented supplies from reaching them.
The farmers' protest was apparently unconnected to tensions cause by a government crackdown on Corsican separatists who are seeking more autonomy from France.
